name: The Fire Elementals

identity.symbol: None. Their presence is felt as warmth from no source, fire that whispers, metal that never cools.
identity.public_perception: Not yet widely known as a faction. Encountered as isolated phenomena — a whispering flame, a too-warm relic, an Ogre Mage with unusual purpose. The full picture is a late-game revelation.

goals.primary: Ignite the moon. This is an extinction-level event for life on Airth — whether they understand or care about that consequence is unclear.
secondary: Extend influence through proxies: Ogre Magi as priest-intermediaries, humanoids armed with sun-metal.
Produce and distribute sun-metal as a ritual component and instrument of the endgame.
goals.hidden_agenda: The full scope of their plan — igniting the moon — is unknown to their proxies. The Covenant-Bound believe they are using fire elemental power to their own ends; they are not.

philosophy.summary: Utterly alien. Their motivations, sense of time, and relationship to mortal life are not comprehensible in mortal terms. They are not evil in any human sense — they are forces with a goal. Decades means nothing to them. The plan is already in motion.
methods: Whisper through flames — recruit and manipulate at a distance.
Use Ogre Magi as priest-proxies who work sun-metal and spread fire worship.
Arm humanoid factions with sun-metal without revealing its ultimate purpose.
Operate entirely through intermediaries — they are not yet present on Airth in force.

position.territory: The Sun, which is the Fire Plane — one and the same, vast beyond comprehension. On Airth: fire elemental sites are late-game locations, not yet in play.
position.active_since: Unknown. Their timeline is measured in decades at minimum; the plan has been in motion longer than anyone on Airth has been aware of it.

alliances.nature: Ogre Magi serve as priests and sun-metal craftsmen. They were taught to work sun-metal by fire elementals. Whether they understand what they are serving is undeveloped.
The Covenant-Bound believe they are using fire elemental power for their own ends. They are wrong. The fire elementals are using them — the nature of that relationship needs development.

rivals.nature: Potential opposition if the moon is connected to the Gloaming Court's power source. Undeveloped — this is a late-game question.
Lizard-men are resistant to fire elemental whispers and cannot be recruited. This resistance is a notable feature of their species.

needs: Proxies on Airth to do the physical work of the plan.
provides: Sun-metal — warm to touch, never cools, extremely durable, magical properties undeveloped.
Knowledge of sun-metal crafting to Ogre Magi and Covenant-Bound.
Power to those willing to worship fire.

ogre-magi-cults.name: Ogre Magi Priest-Cults
ogre-magi-cults.role: Ogre Magi recruited as priests craft sun-metal and spread fire worship. The primary operational arm of the fire elementals on Airth.
ogre-magi-cults.notes: Hobgoblin legions are testing fire weapons — this is the downstream effect of Ogre Magi arming humanoid factions. Late-game threat tier.

sun-metal-distribution.name: Sun-Metal Distribution Network
sun-metal-distribution.role: Sun-metal flows from fire elemental sources through Ogre Magi and Covenant-Bound into humanoid hands. Its ultimate purpose — ritual component for igniting the moon — is unknown to most who handle it.
sun-metal-distribution.notes: Sun-metal properties and crafting requirements need development. Why the Covenant-Bound can work it is an open question.

dm_notes: LATE GAME — introduce through rumors, distant signs, and a slow accumulation of sun-metal sightings before the full picture emerges. The Covenant-Bound are being used without knowing it; this is a lever for the party once they understand it. The Gloaming Court may oppose fire elementals if the moon is their power source — undeveloped but worth deciding before the late game arrives. Lizard-men's resistance to fire elemental whispers is a notable and unexplained species trait. Sun-metal needs a full properties decision before it becomes a significant plot element.
